note: Four hand-authored personas for the Perioperative Optimization composite engine. calculateOptimization(state) is pure (both dates come from the data, never the clock) and returns weeksToSurgery = floor((plannedSurgeryDate - assessmentDate)/7), one gated DomainResult per domain in DOMAIN_ORDER, counts, derived instrument scores (bmi, weightLossPercent, MUST, AUDIT-C, STOP-BANG, DASI, CFS, Fried), computedReadiness (max-grade over domain statuses; Hb < 80 or HbA1c >= 69 force defer-surgery), finalReadiness (the sign-off override if it names a valid band), overrideReason (only when the override actually changed the band), gateDecision, recommendedEarliestSurgeryDate (planned date + the largest positive shortfall) and the flags FOLDED in (push order, stable-sorted high > medium > low). form-app.js merely spreads a wall-clock timestamp over the result. Quirks verified: gating uses weeks >= leadTime, so a 3-week lead with exactly 3 weeks to surgery is in-progress/action-required, not insufficient-time; a 'never' smoker or diabetesType 'none' with null HbA1c makes those domains not-applicable, whereas an ex-smoker is 'optimized' - both count as optimized in counts; each domain evaluator returns only its FIRST matching rule (Hb below the sex threshold hides a low ferritin from R-ANAEMIA-3, though the separate F-IRON-DEFICIENCY-UNTREATED flag still sees it); intentional weight loss > 10% is silent for both MUST and R-NUTRITION-2; STOP-BANG >= 5 is silent when sleepApnoeaDiagnosis is 'yes'; anaemia lead time is 8 weeks unless anaemiaTreatmentRoute is exactly 'intravenous'; the override never touches flags. FIXED 2026-09-06 (was a VERIFIED ENGINE FINDING from 2026-09-04, documented rather than silently patched at the time): five of the eight domains (anaemia, alcohol, nutrition, physical-fitness, cardiorespiratory) used to hard-code `applicable: true` in their evaluator regardless of whether ANY field in that domain was ever answered — only glycaemic-control, smoking, and medication computed `applicable` from real data. `calculateOptimization` over an assessment with nothing entered except the two dates used to report anaemia/alcohol/nutrition/physical-fitness/cardiorespiratory all as status 'optimized', identical to a genuinely-assessed all-clear patient. Fixed by deriving `applicable` per domain from whether any of that domain's own measures are non-null/non-blank — anaemia: hb/ferritin/tsat; alcohol: units/auditC; nutrition: must/pct; physical-fitness: mets/dasi/walk/at; cardiorespiratory: sbp/dbp/ef/stopBang/spo2/asthmaControl/copdControl — mirroring how glycaemic-control/smoking/medication already did it, in both `js/domain-rules.js` and `src/lib/engine/domain-rules.ts`. Confirmed the current `back-end-with-loco` has no scoring logic of its own (JSON-API-only, per this repo's own convention) and no `todo/` prototype exists for this form, so no third stack needed changing despite this file's earlier note assuming otherwise. `computedReadiness` is unaffected either way for a wholly blank assessment — both 'optimized' and 'not-applicable' map to the same 'ready' readiness band, and `counts.optimized` counts both statuses together — the fix's real, visible effect is per-domain transparency in the report/dashboard, not the composite verdict. The fourth persona below pins the fixed behaviour: all eight domains now correctly report 'not-applicable'. All 110 existing Vitest boundary tests for this engine (which all use domains with real answered data) were unaffected and still pass. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas perioperative-optimization --update

personas.name: Ex-smoker with treated iron-deficiency anaemia - IV iron in progress, clinician overrides to ready
personas.description: Non-critical edge case built from boundary values and 'silent' paths. A 47-year-old woman assessed 2026-09-01 for a hysterectomy on 2026-10-15 (44 days, floor -> 6 weeks). Hb 118 fires R-ANAEMIA-2 (< 120 for women) and, because the route is 'intravenous' and treatment has started, the lead time is 4 weeks <= 6 so the domain is 'in-progress'; ferritin 25 is hidden from the rules by the first-match Hb branch and does NOT raise F-IRON-DEFICIENCY-UNTREATED because treatment has started. Ex-smoker -> smoking 'optimized' (not 'not-applicable'); no diabetes with HbA1c null -> glycaemic 'not-applicable'; 14 units/week (rule is > 14) and AUDIT-C 2+1+0 = 3 (rule is >= 4 for women) -> alcohol optimized; 12.1% weight loss recorded as intentional -> MUST 0 (BMI 22.1) and R-NUTRITION-2 suppressed; ACE inhibitor in use WITH an agreed hold plan -> medication optimized with interventionStarted true; STOP-BANG 5 with a confirmed OSA diagnosis on CPAP -> silent; METs 5 / DASI 40 / 6MWT 450 all above threshold; CFS 3 with Fried 1/5 (exhaustion only) -> 'pre-frail'. Expect weeksToSurgery 6, counts optimized 7 / inProgress 1, computedReadiness 'optimization-in-progress', but the sign-off override 'ready' (reason recorded) makes finalReadiness 'ready' with overrideReason populated; gateDecision 'proceed'; recommendedEarliestSurgeryDate ''; flags [].

personas.name: Frail 71-year-old with obstructing colorectal cancer listed in 3 weeks - six domains short of time
personas.description: Critical / highest-severity persona: assessed 2026-09-01 for a major-plus anterior resection on 2026-09-22 (exactly 3 weeks). Anaemia Hb 76 (R-ANAEMIA-5; oral/unspecified route -> 8-week lead, shortfall 5) and ferritin 12 untreated; HbA1c 72 in known type-2 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin with no diabetes-team review (R-GLYC-2, 12-week lead, shortfall 9); current smoker declining cessation (R-SMOKE-1, shortfall 1); AUDIT-C 4+3+3 = 10 with dependence features (R-ALCOHOL-4, shortfall 1); BMI 18.3 + 20.6% unintentional loss -> MUST 4 (R-NUTRITION-1) but a 3-week lead against exactly 3 weeks is NOT short and the dietitian referral is made, so nutrition is 'in-progress'; CPET AT 9.5 (R-FITNESS-4, 6-week lead, shortfall 3); apixaban + empagliflozin + weekly semaglutide with GI symptoms, GLP-1 held per guideline, and no hold plan (R-MEDICATION-1, 1-week lead -> action-required); EF 35 (R-CARDIORESP-3, shortfall 1) alongside BP 184/112, uncontrolled COPD, SpO2 90 and STOP-BANG 6 unassessed; eGFR 24; CFS 7 with Mini-Cog not done and Fried 5/5 frail; previous anaesthetic complication; severe anxiety and positive depression screen; no transport home; capacity concern. Expect weeksToSurgery 3; statuses anaemia/glycaemic-control/smoking/alcohol/physical-fitness/cardiorespiratory insufficient-time, nutrition in-progress, medication action-required; counts 0/1/1/6; computedReadiness 'defer-surgery' (also forced by Hb < 80 and HbA1c >= 69); override 'optimization-required' applied so finalReadiness 'optimization-required' with overrideReason recorded; gateDecision 'accept-unoptimized-risk'; recommendedEarliestSurgeryDate 2026-09-22 + 9 weeks = '2026-11-24'; and 25 flags after the stable sort - 16 high in push order: F-INSUFFICIENT-TIME-TO-OPTIMIZE-001 ('6 domains ... largest shortfall is 9 weeks'), F-SEVERE-ANAEMIA-001, F-HBA1C-ABOVE-THRESHOLD-001, F-SGLT2-INHIBITOR-NOT-HELD-001, F-GLP1-AGONIST-ASPIRATION-RISK-001 (GI-symptoms wording), F-ANTICOAGULATION-PLAN-MISSING-001, F-ACTIVE-SMOKER-MAJOR-SURGERY-001, F-ALCOHOL-DEPENDENCE-RISK-001 (AUDIT-C wording), F-HIGH-MALNUTRITION-RISK-001, F-SEVERE-FRAILTY-001, F-DEHYDRATION-AKI-RISK-001, F-UNCONTROLLED-HYPERTENSION-001, F-CARDIAC-OPTIMIZATION-REQUIRED-001, F-RESPIRATORY-OPTIMIZATION-REQUIRED-001 (SpO2 wording), F-RENAL-OPTIMIZATION-REQUIRED-001, F-PRIOR-ANAESTHETIC-COMPLICATION-001 (with detail); then 9 medium: F-IRON-DEFICIENCY-UNTREATED-001, F-POOR-FUNCTIONAL-CAPACITY-001, F-COGNITIVE-ASSESSMENT-INDICATED-001, F-SARCOPENIA-RISK-001, F-REBOUND-GLYCAEMIC-RISK-001, F-OSA-UNASSESSED-001, F-PSYCHOLOGICAL-SUPPORT-REQUIRED-001 (depression wording), F-SOCIAL-SUPPORT-GAP-001 (transport wording), F-CAPACITY-CONCERN-001. flags.description: 6 domains cannot be optimized before the listed date: anaemia, glycaemic-control, smoking, alcohol, physical-fitness, cardiorespiratory. The largest shortfall is 9 weeks.
flags.suggestedAction: Either move the surgery date to create the window, or record an explicit accept-unoptimized-risk decision at sign-off. Do not proceed believing the patient is optimized.

flags.description: Haemoglobin 76 g/L is below 80.
flags.suggestedAction: Urgent haematology review; consider transfusion. Elective surgery is normally deferred.

flags.description: HbA1c 72 mmol/mol is at or above the CPOC deferral threshold of 69 mmol/mol (8.5%).
flags.suggestedAction: Diabetes-team review. Defer elective surgery unless the delay would itself cause harm.

flags.description: An SGLT2 inhibitor is in use with no agreed hold plan.
flags.suggestedAction: Agree a hold plan with the prescriber. These drugs can precipitate ketoacidosis with a normal blood glucose, so check ketones rather than glucose if the patient is unwell.

flags.description: A GLP-1 receptor agonist is in use with active gastrointestinal symptoms — delayed gastric emptying raises aspiration risk.
flags.suggestedAction: Apply full-stomach precautions: consider withholding the dose per guideline (daily formulations on the day of surgery, weekly formulations one week prior), consider point-of-care gastric ultrasound, and prefer regional anaesthesia where appropriate.

flags.description: An anticoagulant is in use with no agreed hold-and-restart plan.
flags.suggestedAction: Agree the plan with the prescriber, balancing bleeding risk against thrombotic risk. Bridging is not routine and is itself a source of harm.

flags.description: The patient currently smokes and is listed for major surgery.
flags.suggestedAction: Offer cessation support and nicotine replacement now. Four weeks of abstinence measurably reduces respiratory and wound complications.

flags.description: AUDIT-C score 10 indicates a high level of drinking.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer to alcohol services and put a withdrawal-prevention plan in place for the admission.

flags.description: MUST score 4 indicates high malnutrition risk.
flags.suggestedAction: Dietitian referral, food fortification, and oral nutritional supplements; consider immunonutrition before major gastrointestinal surgery.

flags.description: Clinical Frailty Scale 7 indicates severe frailty.
flags.suggestedAction: Involve a perioperative medicine for older people service; revisit shared decision-making, including the option of not operating.

flags.description: Frail patient with GLP-1-related gastrointestinal symptoms plus fasting — elevated risk of dehydration, acute kidney injury, and delirium.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider pre-admission intravenous fluids, minimise fasting duration, and monitor renal function and cognition closely.

flags.description: Blood pressure 184/112 mmHg meets the deferral threshold of 180/110.
flags.suggestedAction: Repeat the measurement, review antihypertensive therapy, and defer elective surgery if it remains above threshold.

flags.description: Ejection fraction 35% is below 40%.
flags.suggestedAction: Cardiology review before surgery; consider enhanced perioperative care and postoperative critical care.

flags.description: Oxygen saturation 90% on room air is below 92%.
flags.suggestedAction: Respiratory review, inhaler technique and adherence check, and a rescue plan before surgery.

flags.description: eGFR 24 ml/min indicates severe renal impairment.
flags.suggestedAction: Renal review; check nephrotoxic medicines, contrast exposure, and fluid plan before surgery.

flags.description: A previous anaesthetic complication is recorded: Post-operative delirium and unplanned ICU admission after hernia repair 2010.
flags.suggestedAction: Retrieve the previous anaesthetic record and involve a consultant anaesthetist in planning well before the date.

flags.description: Ferritin 12 µg/L indicates iron deficiency, and no treatment has been started.
flags.suggestedAction: Start iron replacement and investigate the cause; iron deficiency in an adult may indicate gastrointestinal blood loss.

flags.description: Functional capacity is below the perioperative threshold on at least one measure.
flags.suggestedAction: Offer prehabilitation; consider cardiopulmonary exercise testing and enhanced perioperative care planning.

flags.description: Clinical Frailty Scale 7 — Mini-Cog not yet performed.
flags.suggestedAction: Perform a Mini-Cog and consider a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment before surgery.

flags.description: Frail patient on a GLP-1 receptor agonist — risk of accelerated sarcopenia from combined muscle and fat loss.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer for protein supplementation and resistance-exercise prehabilitation before surgery.

flags.description: A GLP-1 receptor agonist was held or fasting extended in a patient on insulin — risk of rebound hyperglycaemia or hypoglycaemia.
flags.suggestedAction: Agree a perioperative glycaemic monitoring and insulin-adjustment plan with the diabetes team.

flags.description: STOP-BANG score 6 indicates a high probability of obstructive sleep apnoea, which has not been assessed.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer for a sleep study; plan postoperative monitoring and use opioids with caution.

flags.description: The depression screen is positive.
flags.suggestedAction: Offer psychological support as part of multimodal prehabilitation; revisit the shared decision-making conversation.

flags.description: No transport home has been arranged.
flags.suggestedAction: Resolve before the date; day-case surgery normally requires both transport and a responsible adult at home.

flags.description: A concern about capacity to consent is recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Assess capacity for the specific decision, involve a carer or advocate, and plan for postoperative delirium risk.

personas.name: Entirely blank assessment except the two dates - all eight domains not-applicable, not falsely optimized
personas.description: Nothing entered anywhere except the assessment date and the planned surgery date (12 weeks away): pins the 2026-09-06 fix where all eight domain evaluators now correctly derive `applicable` from whether any of their own fields were actually answered. Before the fix, anaemia/alcohol/nutrition/physical-fitness/cardiorespiratory hard-coded applicable:true, so this exact blank state reported 'optimized' on all five (identical to a genuinely-assessed, all-clear patient); now all eight domains correctly report 'not-applicable'. computedReadiness stays 'ready' either way (both 'optimized' and 'not-applicable' map to the same readiness band, and the fleet-wide counts.optimized total is unaffected since it counts both statuses together) — the fix's real, visible effect is per-domain transparency: a report or dashboard reading domain-by-domain status can no longer mistake an unassessed patient for a confirmed-fit one.
